context_requirements: Intact glucocorticoid receptor signaling and coactivator availability
For anti-inflammatory/transrepression effects, an active inflammatory or stress signaling context (e.g., NF-kB, AP-1)
falsifiers: No induction of canonical GR target genes such as TSC22D3, FKBP4, DUSP1, or PER1 at 6 h in any cell line
No dose-dependent or time-dependent transcriptional changes at 10 micromolar in responsive lines
Lack of repression of inflammatory genes (e.g., IL1B, CXCL2, CCL2) in a context where they are induced

evidence.supports: Glucocorticoid receptor agonists act via transactivation and transrepression to mediate anti-inflammatory effects.
Selective GR agonists show anti-inflammatory activity and regulate gene expression.
GR agonist mapracorat inhibits cytokine release and MAPK/NF-kB/AP-1 pathways in human cells.
Dexamethasone induces GR-regulated genes and hepatic steatosis via MED1-dependent transcription.
GR agonists suppress inflammatory cytokine mRNA and modulate osteogenic differentiation in human bone marrow stromal cells.
